page.layout: One page of text. Running head at top centre-left, page number at top right. Main text in one column, with a large centred section heading. Marginal notes in the left margin (faint and illegible) and one note in the right margin.

main_text.p: [illegible, ~20 letters]Christus dives ex se, nulli obstrictus. Nos divi-tes ex ipso, fratribus obstricti.
Christus depauperatus extreme propter nos. Nos tantillum dare gravabimur propter ipsum?
Christus sua paupertate nos ditavit cœlestibus thesauris: Nos gravabimur sublevare inopiam fratrum bonis caducis?
main_text.l: Propositio. Dicam. I. Quomodo Christus dives antequam pauper.
III Quare:& quas divitias paupertate sua nobis conferat.
main_text.head: I. Quomodo Christus fuerit dives, antequam fieret pauper.
main_text.p: Factus est pauper πτωχὸς ὤν. Quomodo & quibus divitiis dives fuerit ante paupertatem, cō-siderandum.

Reiice mundi opinionem, cum divitias vel divitem audit somniantis magnos thesauros & talenta auri, argenti, possessiones fundorum, servorum, &c. vel aliquem Midam, Croesum aut Crassum,&c. quorum historiolas paucis asperge: & ostende eos fuisse divitiarum pauperes servos: quoniam etiam Philosophis pauperes sunt, non qui modicum habent, sed qui plura appetunt.Seneca de pauperte[?] Horum namque fuit insatiabilis cupiditas.

page.notes: Left margin carries several small marginal notes in faint type that cannot be read; only a placeholder is given for the first. Right margin note read as "Seneca de pauperte", the last word doubtful. The Greek word after "Per" is illegible. "Reiice" at the start of the paragraph is uncertain because of the large initial. The number "I." in the Propositio line may be printed as a dotless i. The catchword "seu" is at the right below the last line. Show-through from the reverse is not transcribed.
